title: Day 3 Diagnostic — Daily routines & frequency
purpose: Kiểm tra khả năng mô tả pattern thật, chọn mức tần suất hợp lý, đặt frequency language tự nhiên và chuyển kiến thức Day 1–2 vào routine speech.

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly reuses a Day 1 item to describe a habit?
options: I usually start work around eight.
I start usually work around eight.
Usually I am start work around eight.
I usual start work around eight.
questions.explanation: 'Usually' was introduced on Day 1. With a lexical verb such as 'start', a very common position is before the verb: 'I usually start…'.

questions.prompt: Your morning routine happens on many days but not all of them. Which opening is most appropriately non-absolute?
options: I never start early.
Most days, I start early.
I always start early, except many days.
I must start early.
questions.explanation: 'Most days' describes a strong pattern without claiming that there are no exceptions.

questions.prompt: Why is Present Simple useful in 'I start work at eight' when describing a routine?
options: It means the action is happening at this exact second.
It frames the action as part of the normal/repeated picture.
It always describes the distant past.
It means the action happened only once.
questions.explanation: In routine talk, Present Simple presents an event as a regular pattern or current fact, not as an event currently unfolding.

questions.prompt: You almost never skip breakfast, but it has happened once or twice. Which wording is the best fit?
options: I always skip breakfast.
I hardly ever skip breakfast.
I skip breakfast every day.
I never eat anything ever.
questions.explanation: 'Hardly ever' communicates very low frequency without making the absolute claim carried by 'never'.

questions.prompt: When saying a routine sentence naturally, which strategy is most useful?
options: Give every syllable equal weight.
Delete all small words completely.
Listen for and produce prominent content words while keeping smaller function words lighter.
Speak as fast as possible even if clarity drops.
questions.explanation: English speech often gives more prominence to information-bearing words. Smaller function words may be lighter, but clarity remains the goal.

questions.prompt: Which sentence naturally describes finally finding time for something you had been meaning to do?
options: I get around reading.
I get around to reading in the evening.
I around to read.
I am get to around reading.
questions.explanation: 'Get around to' is followed by a noun or V-ing: 'get around to reading'. It often implies the action was delayed.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best connects Day 2 work identity with today's routine topic?
options: I work mainly on backend systems, so I usually start with focused work before checking messages.
I backend mainly and routine work.
What about you backend every day always?
Actually work is usually identity systems.
questions.explanation: The sentence retrieves the Day 2 frame 'I work mainly on…' and naturally extends it with today's habit frame 'I usually…'.

questions.prompt: Why can 'usually' or 'often' be more useful than an exact percentage in everyday conversation?
options: Because English speakers cannot count.
Because these words efficiently communicate a perceived pattern when exact measurement is unnecessary.
Because frequency words always mean the same percentage.
Because exact numbers are grammatically incorrect.
questions.explanation: Frequency adverbs are intentionally approximate. Their job is often to convey a useful pattern, not a measured statistic.

spokenChallenge.prompt: Speak for 90 seconds about a typical workday. Use at least three different frequency expressions, reuse one Day 2 work/identity frame, explain why one habit matters to you, and include one genuine exception to your normal routine.
